title: A quiet red dwarf
bodyMd: For decades, astronomers searching for potentially habitable planets paid little attention to the small red dwarf star Kerrin-7. Because the star is so dim, its habitable zone, the range of orbits in which a planet could keep liquid water on its surface, lies very close to it, and a planet orbiting that close would be exposed to the violent flares that red dwarfs frequently emit. In 2024, however, a team led by astronomer Oyelaran Adeyemi reported that Kerrin-7 had produced almost no flares during eleven years of monitoring. The team has since begun searching the star's habitable zone for planets.
